summary.intent: Address a pattern of swallowed errors (failed reads treated as missing data) in the Callisto release tool, flagged by Codex review and a subagent sweep, and fix the structural gaps so such bugs stop recurring.
summary.outcome: Opened PR 1 (fix/strict-reads) with a strict_fs helper, a new E310 unreadable-manifest error, a unified strict changeset listing, strict pre.json/config/changelog/apply/init sites, and atomic-write sync error propagation; local `just ci` passed (exit 0, 92.82% coverage). A stacked PR plan for the remaining structural gaps was written, and the user approved the two policy calls (error on a malformed root manifest, reject unstageable symlinked packages).

repo: AGENTS.md requires sibling instances of a bug to be fixed together, not one at a time.
Every new error code needs a row in docs/errors.md; a doc-check test in callisto-model fails otherwise (hit with E310).
Specs in docs/specs/workspace.json mandate the admit-all fallback for malformed membership and symlink following, so changing either is a spec/policy change made in the same PR as the code.
`just ci` includes a cargo fmt check; new files must be formatted or CI fails with exit 1.
Two separate implementations of 'list changesets' existed (aggregate.rs lenient, commands/version.rs strict); the strict one was the template for unification.
Shared test fixtures live in callisto-fixtures (added a LockedDir guard for unsearchable-directory permission tests).
A path beneath a regular file yields NotADirectory, which should count as absent rather than a failed read in strict existence checks.
Git rejects staging a path through a directory symlink (fatal: pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link, exit 128).

code.finding: `if let Ok(editor) = open_cached(..)` drops publish targets on a failed reopen, so the package falls back to PublishTarget::None and silently never publishes.
`if let Ok(m) = open_cached(..)` drops dependency edges on failure, corrupting cascade and publish ordering.
`let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(..) else { continue }` conflates NotFound with EACCES/invalid UTF-8, so unreadable manifests vanish from discovery.
Directory open/sync_all errors after rename are discarded with `let _res`, while the function documents a durable replace.
`entries.flatten()` and `is_file()` drop per-entry errors, so a pending changeset can silently disappear from a release.
An unreadable or unparseable root Cargo.toml or pyproject.toml returns Membership::absent(), which admits every directory.
resolve_commit returns Ok(None) for any non-zero git exit, so a corrupt or shallow state looks like an absent tag and widens inference.
After a 3s reader grace timeout on a child that exited 0, stdout_result.unwrap_or_default() returns success with empty stdout.
`add` writes a generated changeset slug without checking for an existing file, and atomic_write replaces it, so a slug collision can destroy a pending changeset.

workflow: Subagent sweep results were from source tracing only and not reproduced, so they should be treated as leads and verified.
Codex's review separated confirmed release risks from conditional cases and spec-mandated behavior; this triage narrowed the proposal and led to rejecting a blanket lint on Path::exists/.ok().
The plans directory shared across worktrees was off-limits, so the plan was written inside the worktree under a git-excluded path.
Helper-insertion scripts can attach a new function to the wrong doc comment, so check doc attachment after scripted edits.
Fixes for a bug pattern are stacked as separate PRs (instances, then membership, then a total-workspace invariant) with fault-injection tests.

friction: Codex's reported line numbers for walk.rs were off, so the sites had to be re-located.
The first `just ci` run failed only on formatting of the new fixtures file and had to be rerun, costing a long CI cycle.
A scripted helper insertion landed between apply_version_plan and its doc comment and had to be moved.
An existing test exposed that NotADirectory must be treated as absent, requiring a helper revision.
Writes to the shared plans directory were blocked from the worktree.
open_items: PR 2 (discovery-total): typed Membership (absent/unrestricted/restricted/invalid), OpenContext::for_workspace_root returns Result, reject symlinked packages Git can't stage, and flip the spec and tests pinning the old fallback.
PR 3 (workspace-complete): graph build collects unresolved items; Workspace::load errors if any exist, with only `status` allowed a partial scan; fault-injection tests.
PR 4 (write-preflight): validate every target in the plan before the first write.
PR 5 (smaller fixes): no-clobber changeset slugs, TagIndex dropping LastTagSelection.skipped, three-state git probes in GitAccess, runner output truncation, file-mode loss on rewrite.
Independent review of PR 1 still to run after pushing, and remote CI result on PR 1 not yet seen.
Earlier open questions: whether Python-only workspaces move to the sealed multi-job route, plus separate PRs for the pnpm package-manager mismatch and the NAPI path guess.
Codex's missing PyPI digest check finding at the #232/#233 heads remains a separate unresolved release issue.
Shallow-clone guard outside observe_git_commit_trust, and walk diagnostics not shown by version/release, were noted by the sweep but not scheduled.
